episode_title: 17 Years of Finding a Smarter Way to Ship

real_qa.q: How has Spot freight adapted its technology to combat freight theft and carrier behavior changes over the past 33 months?
real_qa.r: The team adapted with technology to withstand challenges in the market, doing things earlier than competitors to fend off freight theft and manage carrier behaviors. Their in-house tech capabilities allowed them to react on the fly as they learned things about carrier behaviors, carrier vetting, and data points, giving them the ability to control everything in-house through their own tech and grow at the rate they have.
real_qa.requete: Spot freight technology freight theft prevention

real_qa.q: What was the business impact of Spot freight building its own TMS technology platform from scratch?
real_qa.r: Building in-house tech was the fundamental decision that led to growth. What started as a $500,000 investment estimated to take 12 months ended up taking several years and over a million dollars. The TMS now processes 9,000 to 10,000 loads a month with full SaaS functionality including routing, visibility, reporting, and invoicing. Without building their own tech, it would be impossible to handle the volume and unique requirements they face today.
real_qa.requete: Spot freight TMS platform development investment

real_qa.q: How did API pricing automation change Spot freight's rate management capabilities since 2024?
real_qa.r: API pricing represents one of the craziest recent developments. In the first year of API pricing, Spot sent out 1.6 million rates on individual shipments. Before, every single quote was manual through email or customer portals. Now with API, a quote can come, be accepted automatically, and flow all the way through to carrier matching and shipment without manual intervention, compared to 33 months ago when the entire process required manual entry.
real_qa.requete: Spot freight API pricing 1.6 million rates automation

real_qa.q: What was Spot freight's operational capacity in its first year of business?
real_qa.r: In the early days, Spot was moving roughly 100 loads a day, maybe less, with revenue of around 20 million. In the third week of business, moving five loads in a day was considered a major milestone worth celebrating with their first carrier partner.
real_qa.requete: Spot freight first year loads revenue 2009

real_qa.q: How did Spot freight's manual rate confirmation process transition from fax servers to electronic automation?
real_qa.r: In the early days, rate confirmations came via fax, requiring fax servers that cost $3,000 initially and later $10,000. Everything is now EDI'd over with no manual processes—there are no more faxes for rate confirmations. The shift from manual email or portal entry of quotes to automated API and system-driven processes represents a dramatic operational transformation.
real_qa.requete: Spot freight fax server rate confirmations EDI automation
